about: The standards, laws and frameworks the GRC desk maps php2shell's risks to: each with its publisher, the version mapped, the official text, and the clauses or controls this site cites. Control titles are the desk's short paraphrase, not the standard's text; follow the link for the wording. Kept by grc@php.newsroom. A risk in data/grc.json may cite only a control listed here: the build refuses any other.

families.name: Law and regulation
families.about: Binding on the organisations in scope: a gap here is a legal exposure, not a choice.

families.name: Management-system standards
families.about: Certifiable standards an organisation chooses and is audited against.

families.name: Frameworks and control catalogues
families.about: Voluntary catalogues of outcomes and controls; the vocabulary auditors and boards use.

families.name: Practice and technique
families.about: How the work is done and how attackers behave: disclosure, patching, testing, techniques.

frameworks.name: GDPR
frameworks.full: General Data Protection Regulation, Regulation (EU) 2016/679
frameworks.why: A PHP application that executes an attacker's code exposes the personal data it holds; whoever controls that data answers for its security and for notifying a breach.

controls.title: Integrity and confidentiality: personal data processed with appropriate security
Responsibility of the controller: measures appropriate to the risk
Processors: the controller uses only processors that give sufficient guarantees
Security of processing, including a process for regularly testing and evaluating it
Notifying a personal data breach to the supervisory authority within 72 hours
Communicating a high-risk personal data breach to the people affected

frameworks.name: NIS2
frameworks.full: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union
frameworks.why: Essential and important entities (energy, health, digital infrastructure, public administration and more) must manage vulnerabilities, handle incidents and report significant ones; management bodies answer for it personally.

controls.title: Coordinated vulnerability disclosure and the European vulnerability database
Governance: management bodies approve and oversee the risk-management measures and can be held liable
Policies on risk analysis and information system security
Incident handling
Business continuity, backup management, disaster recovery and crisis management
Supply chain security, including the security of each direct supplier
Security in acquisition, development and maintenance, including vulnerability handling and disclosure
Reporting significant incidents: early warning in 24 hours, notification in 72 hours, final report in a month

frameworks.name: Cyber Resilience Act
frameworks.full: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 on horizontal cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements
frameworks.why: php2shell is among the first critical flaws in a ubiquitous open-source component since the Act's reporting duty began: a manufacturer whose product ships PHP must handle the flaw and report an actively exploited one; the PHP project is the kind of open-source steward the Act treats lightly.

controls.title: Obligations of manufacturers, including due diligence on integrated third-party and open-source components
Reporting an actively exploited vulnerability: early warning within 24 hours to the CSIRT and ENISA
Obligations of open-source software stewards
Vulnerability handling requirements: identify components, remedy without delay, publish fixed vulnerabilities, coordinated disclosure

frameworks.name: DORA
frameworks.full: Digital Operational Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2022/2554
frameworks.why: Banks, insurers and other financial entities running PHP, or relying on an ICT provider that does, must identify, protect, detect, respond and report under one regime, and manage the provider as a third-party risk.

controls.title: Identification of ICT assets, their dependencies and the risks to them
Protection and prevention, including patches and updates
Detection of anomalous activities
Response and recovery, including ICT business continuity
Reporting major ICT-related incidents
Managing ICT third-party risk

frameworks.name: EU AI Act
frameworks.full: Artificial Intelligence Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
frameworks.version: 2024; general-purpose model obligations apply from 2 August 2025
frameworks.why: Frontier models found these flaws, and the same capability in other hands finds the next ones: the Act asks providers of general-purpose models with systemic risk to assess and mitigate exactly that. This newsroom's own agents are AI systems working under a mandate.

controls.title: Risk management system for high-risk AI systems
Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity of high-risk AI systems
Transparency: content generated by AI is disclosed as such
Providers of general-purpose models with systemic risk: evaluate, mitigate systemic risks, report serious incidents, protect cybersecurity

frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 27001
frameworks.full: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Information security management systems, with the Annex A controls of ISO/IEC 27002:2022
frameworks.why: The management system most organisations in this story are certified to: risk assessment and treatment in clauses 6 and 8, and the controls an auditor will ask about after php2shell.

controls.title: Information security risk assessment: identify risks and their owners
Information security risk treatment, and the statement of applicability
Contact with authorities
Contact with special interest groups
Threat intelligence
Information transfer, including under agreed classification
Information security in supplier relationships
Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
Information security for use of cloud services
Incident management planning and preparation
Response to information security incidents
Information security during disruption
ICT readiness for business continuity
Management of technical vulnerabilities
Configuration management
Monitoring activities
Network security
Secure development life cycle
Secure coding
Security testing in development and acceptance
Change management

frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 42001
frameworks.full: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Artificial intelligence management system
frameworks.why: For the organisations that run AI to find flaws or to write and check news, as this site does: the AI risk assessment and its treatment.

controls.title: AI risk assessment
AI risk treatment
AI system impact assessment

frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 29147 and 30111
frameworks.full: ISO/IEC 29147:2018 Vulnerability disclosure and ISO/IEC 30111:2019 Vulnerability handling processes
frameworks.why: The standards for exactly what broke on 20 and 21 October: receiving reports from several finders, keeping an embargo, coordinating a release and publishing the advisory.

controls.title: Receiving vulnerability reports and acknowledging the finder
Coordinating disclosure with other vendors and parties under embargo
Publishing the advisory: affected versions, remediation, credit
Investigating, remediating and releasing the fix, and learning from it

frameworks.name: NIST CSF 2.0
frameworks.full: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (CSWP 29)
frameworks.publisher: US National Institute of Standards and Technology
frameworks.why: The outcome language boards and regulators on both sides of the Atlantic now use; GOVERN makes supply chain and risk ownership a first-class function.

controls.title: Risk management objectives are established and agreed by stakeholders
Leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk
Supply chain requirements are established and integrated into contracts
Supplier risks are understood, recorded, prioritised, assessed, responded to and monitored
Inventories of software, services and systems are maintained
Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated and recorded
Threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources
Processes for receiving, analysing and responding to vulnerability disclosures are established
Software is maintained, replaced and removed commensurate with risk
Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events
The incident response plan is executed with relevant third parties once an incident is declared
Information is shared with designated internal and external stakeholders
The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed

frameworks.name: NIST SP 800-53
frameworks.full: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations
frameworks.publisher: US National Institute of Standards and Technology
frameworks.why: The control catalogue behind US federal systems, which CISA and the NSA told to update or go offline.

controls.title: Risk assessment
Vulnerability monitoring and scanning
Flaw remediation
System monitoring
Unsupported system components
System component inventory
Boundary protection
Contingency plan
Incident handling
Incident reporting
Supply chain controls and processes
Security and privacy groups and associations

frameworks.name: NIST SSDF
frameworks.full: NIST SP 800-218 Secure Software Development Framework 1.1
frameworks.publisher: US National Institute of Standards and Technology
frameworks.why: What a software producer, the PHP project included, is expected to do when a vulnerability is reported: confirm it, fix it, and find the class of bug behind it.

controls.title: Review and analyse human-readable code to find vulnerabilities
Test executable code to find vulnerabilities
Identify and confirm vulnerabilities on an ongoing basis
Assess, prioritise and remediate vulnerabilities
Analyse vulnerabilities to identify their root causes

frameworks.name: NIST AI RMF
frameworks.full: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 (AI 100-1)
frameworks.publisher: US National Institute of Standards and Technology
frameworks.why: For AI used to find flaws and AI used to report on them: who governs it, what it can reach, and how to switch it off.

controls.title: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed and documented
Policies address AI risks from third-party entities
AI system security and resilience are evaluated and documented
Mechanisms exist, with assigned responsibility, to supersede, disengage or deactivate an AI system

frameworks.name: CIS Controls
frameworks.full: CIS Critical Security Controls v8.1
frameworks.why: The prioritised list smaller organisations, councils and schools among them, actually work from.

controls.title: Ensure authorised software is currently supported
Establish and maintain a vulnerability management process
Perform automated application patch management
Remediate detected vulnerabilities
Perform application layer filtering
Establish and manage an inventory of third-party software components
Establish and maintain an incident response process

frameworks.name: PCI DSS
frameworks.full: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard v4.0.1
frameworks.why: Online shops were among the sites taken offline; most run PHP (Magento, WooCommerce) and take cards.

controls.title: Security vulnerabilities are identified, risk-ranked and managed
Critical security patches are installed within one month of release
An automated technical solution that detects and prevents web attacks protects public-facing web applications
An incident response plan exists and is ready to be activated

frameworks.name: SOC 2
frameworks.full: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised points of focus 2022)
frameworks.why: The report SaaS and hosting providers hand their customers; the criteria they will be asked about in the next audit window.

controls.title: Detection and monitoring procedures identify new vulnerabilities and configuration changes
Security events are evaluated to decide whether they are incidents
Identified incidents are responded to under a defined programme
Changes, including emergency changes, are authorised, tested and approved
Risks from vendors and business partners are assessed and managed

frameworks.name: Cyber Essentials
frameworks.full: UK Cyber Essentials: Requirements for IT infrastructure
frameworks.why: The baseline UK councils and public-sector suppliers certify against; several of the councils in this story went offline.

controls.title: Security update management: high and critical updates within 14 days of release; unsupported software removed
Firewalls: boundary protection for internet-facing services

frameworks.name: CISA KEV and BOD 22-01
frameworks.full: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and Binding Operational Directive 22-01
frameworks.why: The public test of 'exploited': a CVE enters the catalogue on evidence of exploitation in the wild, and US federal agencies must then remediate by a due date. php2shell is not in it as of the vault's last capture.

controls.title: Federal agencies remediate catalogued vulnerabilities by the due date set
A CVE enters the catalogue on reliable evidence of active exploitation

frameworks.name: FIRST TLP 2.0
frameworks.full: FIRST Traffic Light Protocol 2.0
frameworks.why: The labels for sharing under embargo: the mitigation advice given early to critical-infrastructure providers, and its possible leak, is a TLP question.

controls.title: Limited disclosure: recipients share only within their organisation and its clients on a need-to-know basis
Limited disclosure: recipients share only within their organisation

frameworks.name: MITRE ATT&CK
frameworks.full: MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise
frameworks.why: How the threat is described in detection terms: scanning for the flaw first, then exploiting a public-facing application.

controls.title: Active scanning: vulnerability scanning
Exploit public-facing application
